jobDescription: The warehouse scheduling product helps distribution centres plan dock slots and labour shifts. The Customer Success Specialist onboards new sites, runs the quarterly health check with each customer, coordinates escalations with support and product, and is expected to raise the share of sites using automated slot allocation, reported against the customer success team's quarterly baseline.
requirements: Onboards new distribution-centre sites onto the scheduling product and tracks onboarding milestones.
Runs the quarterly health check with each assigned customer and records actions.
Raises the share of assigned sites using automated slot allocation, reported against the quarterly baseline.
Coordinates escalations with support and product and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each customer at quarter-end.

evidence.text: Onboarded fourteen distribution-centre sites across four customers onto the scheduling product, tracking each site's milestones (dock configuration, shift templates, first automated week) in the onboarding tracker.
Ran the quarterly health check with each of my nine assigned customers, walking through slot utilisation and open tickets and recording agreed actions in the account notes.

Automated slot allocation was in use at 21 of my 32 assigned sites at the end of Q2, up from 12 of 32 at the end of Q4 the previous year, according to the customer success adoption dashboard against the team's quarterly baseline of 12 sites.
Coordinated escalations with support and product through the escalation board; fixes and roadmap commitments were decided by the product manager.
Wrote the quarter-end account notes for each customer, listing open limitations (for example sites still on manual dock booking) and the hand-over points for the account manager.

Work sample: the adoption dashboard export for my assigned sites (sites on automated allocation per quarter, baseline line) and one quarter-end account note, with the dashboard export identifiers as a verification trail.
Reference call with former customer success manager: confirmed the adoption figures come from the team dashboard, the count of assigned sites, and the employment dates.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate is available for an on-site session and has no restrictions on travel to customer sites.

propositions.text: The candidate onboarded fourteen distribution-centre sites onto the scheduling product and tracked their milestones in the onboarding tracker.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the onboarding work directly.

propositions.text: The candidate ran quarterly health checks with nine assigned customers and recorded agreed actions in the account notes.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the health-check work.

propositions.text: Automated slot allocation rose from 12 of 32 assigned sites to 21 of 32 between Q4 and Q2 according to the adoption dashboard, against a baseline of 12 sites.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the figures, the period, the baseline and the source; the work sample and reference confirm them.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions for each customer are only partly documented in the quarter-end account notes.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the adoption figures as stated for the assigned sites and period; do not extend them to the whole customer base.
followUpTargets: Ask how hand-over points were recorded for customers at quarter-end.
